name: Complete Blood Count with ESR (CBC + ESR)
measure: Counts red cells, white cells and platelets and measures erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
why: Assessment of anaemia, infection, inflammation or general blood health.
limitation: An elevated ESR is nonspecific and does not identify the cause of inflammation.
special: CBC and ESR provide different information; neither alone confirms an infection.
related: CBC, ESR and peripheral smear are not interchangeable.

name: Blood Glucose (Fasting, PP or Random)
measure: Measures glucose in plasma at a specified collection time.
why: Diabetes screening or monitoring under clinical advice.
fasting: For fasting glucose, follow an 8-hour fast; PP samples need the prescribed after-meal interval, and random samples generally require no fast.
limitation: Fasting, post-meal and random results have different interpretation thresholds.
special: State which glucose sample you need when booking; these are alternative collection timings, not three tests for ₹20.
related: HbA1c reflects longer-term glycaemia, while plasma glucose reflects the sampled time.

name: Glycated Haemoglobin (HbA1c)
measure: Estimates average blood-glucose exposure over roughly the preceding 2–3 months.
why: Screening, diagnosis in suitable settings, or monitoring diabetes.
fasting: Fasting is not usually needed for HbA1c alone.
limitation: Anaemia, haemoglobin variants, recent transfusion and changes in red-cell turnover can affect interpretation.
special: HbA1c does not show immediate glucose changes or detect acute hypoglycaemia.
related: A clinician may also request fasting glucose or an oral glucose tolerance test.

name: Lipid Profile
measure: Assesses cholesterol fractions and triglycerides to support cardiovascular risk assessment.
why: Cholesterol screening and cardiovascular risk evaluation.
fasting: Fasting requirements vary; a non-fasting sample is often acceptable, but fasting may be requested for high triglycerides or specific clinical needs.
limitation: Risk depends on age, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking and other factors—not cholesterol alone.
special: LDL calculated from a lipid profile can differ from a directly measured LDL test.
related: Discuss lipid results in the context of overall cardiovascular risk.

name: Liver Function Test (LFT)
measure: Panel listed as ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, total/direct bilirubin, albumin and protein.
why: Investigation or monitoring of suspected liver or biliary problems.
fasting: Often no fasting is required; follow any clinician or laboratory instructions for the ordered panel.
limitation: Abnormal liver enzymes do not by themselves determine a specific diagnosis or liver function.
special: Confirm exact analytes included in the ₹360 panel before sample collection.
related: Interpret results alongside symptoms, medicines and any imaging.

name: Serum Creatinine
measure: Measures blood creatinine, which is commonly used to estimate kidney filtration (eGFR).
why: Assessment of kidney function or monitoring medicines and chronic conditions.
limitation: Muscle mass, diet and some medicines can affect creatinine; eGFR may require age and sex.
special: A single creatinine result cannot establish chronic kidney disease.
related: Urine albumin-creatinine ratio may add important kidney information.

name: Blood Urea / BUN
measure: Measures urea nitrogen or urea in blood; reporting units vary by laboratory.
why: Kidney assessment or evaluation of hydration and protein metabolism.
fasting: Usually no fasting is needed unless combined with other fasting investigations.
limitation: Urea may rise with dehydration or dietary protein and is not a stand-alone kidney diagnosis.
special: BUN and urea values are related but differ numerically when reported in different units.
related: Creatinine and electrolytes can help give a fuller kidney assessment.

name: Urine Routine & Microscopy
measure: Checks urine chemistry and microscopic elements such as red/white cells, crystals and casts.
why: Symptoms of urinary disorders or evaluation of kidney or metabolic conditions.
limitation: A clean-catch midstream specimen in a sterile container helps reduce contamination.
special: A routine urine test does not replace a urine culture when infection confirmation is required.
related: Menstrual contamination and delayed transport can alter urine findings.

name: Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH)
measure: Measures TSH, a pituitary hormone used to assess thyroid regulation.
why: Initial evaluation or monitoring of thyroid dysfunction.
limitation: TSH can be affected by pregnancy, medication and acute illness; free T4 may be needed.
special: If taking thyroid tablets, follow your clinician's advice on timing relative to collection.
related: TSH alone does not measure free thyroid-hormone concentrations.

name: Thyroid Function Test (Total T3, T4 & TSH)
measure: Measures total T3, total T4 and TSH as listed in the offer.
why: Further assessment of thyroid function where the clinician requests total hormones.
limitation: Total thyroid hormone results are influenced by binding proteins and may differ from free-hormone results.
special: This ₹190 panel specifies total T3/T4; it is different from the free T3/free T4 panel.
related: Biotin supplements can interfere with some immunoassays—tell the laboratory.

name: Serum Electrolytes (Na, K, Cl)
measure: Measures sodium, potassium and chloride in blood.
why: Assessment of fluid balance, kidney conditions or relevant medicines.
limitation: Haemolysis during collection can falsely increase potassium; urgent abnormalities need medical review.
special: This panel does not necessarily include calcium, bicarbonate or magnesium.
related: Interpret electrolytes with renal function, symptoms and medicines.

name: ABO Blood Group & Rh Typing
measure: Determines ABO blood group and RhD status.
why: Pregnancy, transfusion planning or when blood grouping is required.
limitation: Blood group reports do not substitute for crossmatching before transfusion.
special: Weak or discrepant Rh typing needs established laboratory resolution procedures.
related: Use an authorised transfusion service for urgent transfusion decisions.

name: Vitamin D 25-Hydroxy
measure: Measures serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the usual marker of vitamin D status.
why: Assessment of deficiency risk in appropriate clinical settings.
limitation: Vitamin D level must be interpreted alongside symptoms, risk factors and sometimes calcium/PTH.
special: Routine testing is not necessary for everyone without a clinical indication.
related: Do not start high-dose supplements solely from online advice.

name: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
measure: Measures vitamin B12 in serum.
why: Investigation of anaemia, neuropathy or nutritional and absorption concerns.
fasting: Fasting requirements vary by laboratory; ask before attending.
limitation: Recent supplementation can affect vitamin B12 levels; borderline results may need further evaluation.
special: A normal B12 level does not always exclude functional deficiency.
related: Folate and CBC are commonly reviewed alongside B12.

name: Serum Ferritin
measure: Measures ferritin, a marker of iron stores that can also rise with inflammation.
why: Evaluation of suspected iron deficiency or iron overload.
limitation: Ferritin may be high during inflammation even when iron availability is low.
special: Ferritin alone cannot explain every type of anaemia.
related: CBC and transferrin saturation may provide further context.

name: Iron Studies (Iron, TIBC, Saturation)
measure: Measures iron, iron-binding capacity and calculated transferrin saturation as listed.
why: Assessment of iron deficiency or iron overload with clinical context.
fasting: Morning collection or temporary fasting may be requested; confirm local method.
limitation: Serum iron fluctuates during the day and is altered by recent iron intake.
special: Confirm the listed components, including whether ferritin is separate.
related: Clinicians often compare iron studies with ferritin and CBC.

name: C-Reactive Protein (CRP), Quantitative
measure: Measures C-reactive protein, a nonspecific inflammatory marker.
why: Assessment of inflammation or response to treatment.
limitation: Raised CRP does not establish bacterial infection or locate its source.
special: Standard CRP and high-sensitivity CRP are different tests for different clinical uses.
related: Interpret CRP along with symptoms, examination and other tests.

name: Serum Uric Acid
measure: Measures urate in blood.
why: Evaluation of gout, kidney stones or relevant metabolic conditions.
fasting: Fasting is often not essential; follow clinician instructions.
limitation: Urate can be normal during an acute gout attack; high urate alone does not diagnose gout.
special: Diet, dehydration and some medicines may alter results.
related: Gout diagnosis depends on the full clinical picture.

name: Serum Calcium, Total
measure: Measures total blood calcium, including protein-bound and free calcium.
why: Investigation of bone, parathyroid or calcium-balance problems.
limitation: Total calcium is influenced by albumin; ionised calcium may be requested in select situations.
special: Total calcium and ionised calcium are not the same measurement.
related: Interpret the result with albumin and clinical context.

name: Serum Phosphate
measure: Measures inorganic phosphate in blood.
why: Assessment of renal or mineral/bone disorders.
fasting: Usually no fasting is needed unless requested.
limitation: Phosphate may fluctuate with meals, time of day and kidney function.
special: Phosphate is different from serum calcium and is regulated with PTH/vitamin D.
related: Clinical context determines whether retesting is needed.

name: Total Immunoglobulin E (IgE)
measure: Measures total IgE concentration in serum.
why: Selected allergy or immunology investigations.
limitation: High total IgE alone cannot diagnose an allergy to a specific substance.
special: Normal total IgE does not exclude allergic disease.
related: Specific-IgE tests or clinical allergy evaluation may be needed.

name: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg)
measure: Detects hepatitis B surface antigen in blood.
why: Hepatitis B screening or work-up when clinically indicated.
limitation: A reactive screening result requires evaluation under the applicable testing algorithm.
special: HBsAg alone does not show immunity or fully stage hepatitis B infection.
related: Anti-HBs, anti-HBc and HBV DNA may be relevant depending on context.

name: Hepatitis C Antibody (Anti-HCV)
measure: Detects antibodies to hepatitis C virus.
why: Hepatitis C exposure screening under clinical guidance.
limitation: A positive antibody result does not by itself establish current active infection.
special: HCV RNA testing is usually used to determine current infection after a reactive antibody result.
related: A negative antibody test very early after exposure may need follow-up.

name: HIV 1/2 Antigen-Antibody, Fourth Generation
measure: Screens for HIV-1/2 antibodies and p24 antigen using a fourth-generation assay.
why: HIV screening after possible exposure or for other indicated purposes.
limitation: Detection depends on time after exposure and the assay's window period.
special: Follow the applicable NACO testing and confirmation algorithm; no single reactive screen establishes a diagnosis.
related: Recent exposure may require further assessment or repeat testing.

name: Dengue NS1 Antigen & IgM/IgG Antibodies (ELISA)
measure: Tests dengue NS1 antigen and dengue IgM/IgG antibodies as listed in the combination offer.
why: Investigation of suspected dengue based on symptoms and illness day.
limitation: Test performance depends on the day of illness; a negative result does not automatically rule out dengue.
special: Confirm the exact combination and methods before booking.
related: Warning signs such as bleeding, severe abdominal pain or lethargy need urgent evaluation.

name: Malaria Rapid Antigen (HRP2/pLDH)
measure: Uses rapid antigens to support detection of malaria parasites.
why: Investigation of fever when malaria is suspected.
limitation: Negative rapid tests can miss some malaria cases, depending on parasite burden or species.
special: Blood-smear microscopy or repeat testing may be required under clinical advice.
related: Severe illness or suspected malaria needs prompt medical assessment.

name: Prothrombin Time / INR
measure: Measures clotting time via the extrinsic pathway and reports INR where applicable.
why: Monitoring warfarin or evaluation of selected clotting disorders.
limitation: INR targets depend on the individual indication; do not adjust anticoagulants yourself.
special: Sample collection requires correct citrate-tube fill for reliable interpretation.
related: Tell the lab about anticoagulant medicines.

name: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT)
measure: Measures clotting time through the intrinsic/common pathways.
why: Assessment of specific coagulation disorders or anticoagulant monitoring.
limitation: aPTT may be affected by anticoagulants, sample handling and some factor deficiencies.
special: aPTT and PT/INR investigate different parts of coagulation.
related: Abnormal bleeding needs clinical review, not self-interpretation.

name: D-Dimer
measure: Measures fibrin breakdown products in blood.
why: Selected evaluation pathways for suspected thrombosis, together with clinical probability.
limitation: D-dimer may rise for many reasons; an elevated value alone does not confirm a clot.
special: Chest pain, sudden breathlessness or stroke-like symptoms require emergency care; do not wait for outpatient testing.
related: Use with clinician-assessed risk and appropriate imaging where required.

name: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH)
measure: Measures LDH, an enzyme found in many tissues.
why: Assessment of tissue injury or selected haematological conditions.
limitation: Haemolysis during collection can falsely raise LDH.
special: An isolated high LDH does not identify the affected organ.
related: Other targeted tests are needed to determine the cause.

name: Serum Amylase
measure: Measures serum amylase enzyme activity.
why: Evaluation of suspected pancreatic or salivary-gland disease.
fasting: Fasting requirements vary; confirm before collection.
limitation: Amylase can rise for causes other than pancreatitis.
special: A normal amylase does not fully exclude pancreatitis depending on timing.
related: Lipase is often considered alongside or instead of amylase.

name: Serum Lipase
measure: Measures lipase enzyme activity.
why: Investigation of suspected acute pancreatitis when clinically indicated.
fasting: Fasting is not always required; follow local collection advice.
limitation: Raised lipase may occur in non-pancreatic conditions and needs clinical interpretation.
special: Severe upper abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or collapse requires urgent assessment.
related: Diagnosis of pancreatitis uses clinical findings and sometimes imaging.

name: Creatine Phosphokinase (CK/CPK), Total
measure: Measures total creatine kinase enzyme activity.
why: Assessment of muscle injury or selected neuromuscular conditions.
limitation: Strenuous exercise, injections and muscle injury can increase CK.
special: Total CK is not a reliable stand-alone test to diagnose a heart attack.
related: Discuss recent exercise and medicines such as statins with the clinician.

name: Rheumatoid Factor (RF)
measure: Measures rheumatoid factor antibodies.
why: Evaluation of inflammatory arthritis with history and examination.
limitation: Rheumatoid factor can be positive without rheumatoid arthritis, and negative in some affected patients.
special: Anti-CCP antibodies and inflammatory markers may be useful in context.
related: Do not diagnose rheumatoid arthritis from one test.

name: Anti-Streptolysin O (ASO) Titre
measure: Measures antibodies against streptolysin O following group A streptococcal exposure.
why: Assessment of possible preceding streptococcal infection in relevant conditions.
limitation: ASO titre rises after infection and is not an acute throat-swab substitute.
special: A single ASO value often needs clinical context and possibly paired titres.
related: Anti-DNase B may be considered in selected cases.

name: Serum Prolactin
measure: Measures prolactin hormone in blood.
why: Work-up of irregular periods, galactorrhoea or selected pituitary concerns.
fasting: Fasting is not always essential; morning, rested collection may be preferred.
limitation: Stress, exercise, pregnancy and certain medications can raise prolactin.
special: Tell the lab about biotin supplements and prescribed medicines.
related: Mild elevations may warrant repeat sampling under advice.

name: Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
measure: Measures pituitary follicle-stimulating hormone.
why: Assessment of fertility, menstrual, menopausal or selected gonadal conditions.
limitation: In menstruating patients, menstrual-cycle day affects FSH interpretation.
special: Record the cycle day and relevant medications when booking.
related: FSH is interpreted with clinical history and sometimes LH/oestradiol.

name: Luteinising Hormone (LH)
measure: Measures pituitary luteinising hormone.
why: Investigation of menstrual, ovulatory or gonadal conditions.
limitation: LH rises sharply around ovulation; a single result depends on cycle timing.
special: Cycle day, sex and hormonal medicines affect interpretation.
related: LH is often assessed with FSH and other hormones.

name: Total Testosterone
measure: Measures total testosterone including protein-bound hormone.
why: Assessment of androgen-related symptoms under clinical guidance.
fasting: Fasting or early-morning collection may be recommended depending on clinical question and laboratory protocol.
limitation: Testosterone varies by time of day; a low value generally needs appropriate repeat confirmation.
special: Total testosterone is not the same as free testosterone.
related: Interpret results with sex, age, symptoms and SHBG where needed.

name: Beta hCG (Quantitative)
measure: Measures beta human chorionic gonadotropin in blood.
why: Early pregnancy evaluation or monitoring in selected clinical situations.
limitation: Serial beta hCG changes may matter more than one isolated measurement.
special: A single hCG value cannot determine pregnancy location or viability.
related: Pain or bleeding in pregnancy requires timely medical care.

name: Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA)
measure: Measures CEA, a tumour-associated marker used mainly in specified monitoring contexts.
why: Follow-up in selected cancers when requested by an oncologist.
limitation: CEA is not suitable as a stand-alone general cancer-screening test.
special: Smoking and benign conditions can influence CEA.
related: Cancer diagnosis requires appropriate clinical assessment and other investigations.

name: Cancer Antigen 125 (CA-125)
measure: Measures CA-125 protein in blood.
why: Monitoring or investigating selected gynaecological conditions when clinically indicated.
limitation: CA-125 can rise in benign conditions such as menstruation or endometriosis.
special: CA-125 alone cannot screen for or diagnose ovarian cancer reliably.
related: Ultrasound and clinical assessment may be required.

name: Urine Albumin-Creatinine Ratio (ACR)
measure: Measures urinary albumin relative to creatinine to assess albumin leakage.
why: Screening/monitoring kidney disease especially with diabetes or hypertension.
fasting: No fasting is generally needed; early-morning urine is often preferred.
limitation: Fever, strenuous exercise or urinary infection may transiently elevate urine ACR.
special: Repeat confirmation may be advised for an abnormal result.
related: eGFR and urine ACR provide complementary kidney-risk information.

name: Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA), Total
measure: Measures total PSA in blood.
why: Selected assessment of prostate conditions after shared decision-making.
limitation: PSA may rise from benign enlargement, inflammation or recent instrumentation.
special: An elevated PSA does not by itself diagnose prostate cancer.
related: Discuss timing after infection or instrumentation with the clinician.

name: Folic Acid (Serum Folate)
measure: Measures folate concentration in serum.
why: Evaluation of possible folate deficiency or selected anaemia.
fasting: Fasting may be requested; follow the laboratory's method-specific instructions.
limitation: Recent folic-acid supplements or meals can influence serum folate.
special: Folate deficiency and B12 deficiency can have overlapping blood findings.
related: Assess B12 status as clinically indicated before high-dose folate.

name: VDRL Test
measure: Performs a non-treponemal serological test used in syphilis evaluation.
why: Syphilis screening or follow-up as directed by a clinician.
limitation: Reactive VDRL generally requires evaluation with an appropriate treponemal test.
special: False-positive reactions can occur; titres and clinical context matter.
related: Use the appropriate algorithm for confirmation and follow-up.

name: TyphiDot IgM/IgG
measure: Detects IgM/IgG antibodies related to Salmonella Typhi.
why: Limited adjunctive assessment of suspected enteric fever.
limitation: TyphiDot antibody testing has limitations and should not replace clinical evaluation or blood culture.
special: Blood culture, especially before antibiotics, is preferred for confirmatory diagnosis when feasible.
related: Do not delay evaluation of persistent fever.

name: Thyroid Function Panel (Free T3, Free T4, TSH)
measure: Measures free T3, free T4 and TSH.
why: Assessment of thyroid function when free hormones are clinically required.
limitation: Biotin and certain drugs can interfere with some thyroid immunoassays.
special: This ₹330 panel measures free T3/free T4, unlike the ₹190 total T3/T4 panel.
related: Pregnancy and acute illness may change thyroid test interpretation.

name: Platelet Count
measure: Counts platelets in blood.
why: Evaluation of bleeding risk or monitoring low/high platelet counts.
limitation: Platelet clumping can produce a falsely low automated count.
special: Bleeding symptoms or very low results require prompt clinical review.
related: A blood smear may be needed to verify unexpected results.

name: Haemoglobin (Hb)
measure: Measures haemoglobin concentration in blood.
why: Assessment of anaemia or monitoring relevant treatment.
limitation: Low haemoglobin indicates anaemia but not its cause.
special: Interpret with age, sex, pregnancy and CBC indices where relevant.
related: Ferritin, B12 or other tests may be needed based on clinical context.

name: Complete Haemogram (CBC, ESR & Peripheral Smear)
measure: Combines CBC, ESR and peripheral-smear examination as advertised.
why: Assessment of anaemia, blood-cell abnormalities or inflammation.
limitation: Peripheral smear findings require clinical interpretation and are not a diagnosis by themselves.
special: Confirm the smear review scope before booking the ₹230 package.
related: CBC and smear results may warrant further directed tests.

name: Absolute Eosinophil Count (AEC)
measure: Measures absolute eosinophil concentration in blood.
why: Evaluation of eosinophilia with possible allergic, drug or parasitic causes.
limitation: Elevated eosinophils do not identify a specific allergy or infection.
special: AEC should be interpreted with CBC and symptoms.
related: Other testing depends on the clinical history.

name: Bilirubin, Total & Direct
measure: Measures total and direct bilirubin; indirect may be calculated from the difference.
why: Investigation of jaundice or selected liver/biliary conditions.
fasting: Fasting is often not essential, although the lab may advise preparation.
limitation: Bilirubin interpretation depends on direct versus indirect predominance.
special: Bilirubin by itself cannot determine the cause of jaundice.
related: Liver enzymes and clinical evaluation may be needed.

name: Serum Magnesium
measure: Measures magnesium concentration in blood.
why: Assessment of electrolyte disturbances or selected neuromuscular symptoms.
limitation: Serum magnesium may not perfectly reflect total-body stores.
special: Haemolysis can interfere with some magnesium measurements.
related: Potassium and calcium may be checked as clinically indicated.

name: Serum Iron
measure: Measures circulating serum iron concentration.
why: Part of evaluation of suspected abnormal iron status.
fasting: Collection time and fasting may matter; check with the laboratory.
limitation: Serum iron varies during the day and does not assess iron stores by itself.
special: Ferritin and transferrin saturation provide complementary information.
related: Avoid interpreting isolated serum iron as a diagnosis of iron deficiency.

name: Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT / SGPT)
measure: Measures ALT enzyme activity in blood.
why: Assessment of liver-cell injury or monitoring medicines.
limitation: ALT may rise with multiple liver and non-liver conditions.
special: ALT alone does not measure overall liver function or disease severity.
related: AST, bilirubin and other tests may be considered.

name: Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST / SGOT)
measure: Measures AST enzyme activity in blood.
why: Assessment of possible liver or muscle injury.
limitation: AST is present in muscle and other tissues, so it is not liver-specific.
special: Recent strenuous exercise may affect AST.
related: ALT and other markers aid interpretation.

name: Anti-Thyroid Peroxidase Antibodies (Anti-TPO)
measure: Measures antibodies against thyroid peroxidase.
why: Assessment of suspected autoimmune thyroid disease.
limitation: Positive anti-TPO antibodies support autoimmune thyroid disease but do not alone measure thyroid function.
special: TSH and free T4 show hormone status, whereas anti-TPO is an antibody test.
related: Treatment decisions depend on thyroid function and clinical context.

name: Potassium (Serum / Plasma)
measure: Measures potassium electrolyte concentration.
why: Assessment of electrolyte disorders and relevant treatments.
limitation: Collection-related haemolysis can falsely elevate potassium.
special: Severe potassium imbalance can be dangerous; urgent review may be needed.
related: Interpret with kidney function, medicines and ECG when indicated.

name: Renal Profile (Urea, Creatinine, Uric Acid, Electrolytes)
measure: Panel advertised as urea, creatinine, uric acid and electrolytes.
why: Basic evaluation of kidney-related measurements.
fasting: Fasting is usually not needed unless ordered with other fasting tests.
limitation: Normal blood tests do not necessarily exclude early kidney damage.
special: Confirm which electrolytes are in the ₹320 renal profile before booking.
related: Urine ACR and calculated eGFR may add important information.

name: LDL Cholesterol, Direct
measure: Directly measures low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.
why: Assessment of lipid-associated cardiovascular risk where direct LDL is indicated.
fasting: Fasting often is not required, depending on the method and clinical request.
limitation: Direct LDL differs from calculated LDL reported in many lipid panels.
special: LDL treatment targets depend on individual cardiovascular risk.
related: A full lipid profile and risk assessment may still be needed.

name: Troponin I, Quantitative
measure: Measures cardiac troponin I concentration.
why: Clinician-led evaluation of suspected heart-muscle injury.
limitation: Troponin elevations indicate myocardial injury, not necessarily a heart attack; serial testing and ECG may be required.
special: If chest pain, sweating or severe breathlessness is present, go to emergency care instead of booking routine home collection.
related: Troponin is time-sensitive and needs urgent clinical interpretation.

name: Serum Cortisol (AM / PM)
measure: Measures cortisol at a specified morning or evening collection time.
why: Assessment of selected adrenal or endocrine conditions.
fasting: Fasting needs depend on the requested endocrine protocol.
limitation: Cortisol has a daily rhythm, so collection time is essential for interpretation.
special: Specify AM or PM and record relevant steroid medicines, without stopping them unless advised.
related: An isolated cortisol value may not be diagnostic.

name: Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase (GGT)
measure: Measures GGT enzyme activity in blood.
why: Assessment of hepatobiliary abnormalities or follow-up.
fasting: No fasting is usually required unless combined tests specify it.
limitation: GGT is sensitive but nonspecific and may rise with medications or alcohol exposure.
special: GGT alone cannot establish a diagnosis of liver disease.
related: Interpret alongside ALP, ALT, AST and clinical history.

name: Serum Total Protein
measure: Measures total serum protein, mainly albumin and globulins.
why: Assessment of selected liver, kidney or nutritional conditions.
limitation: An abnormal total protein does not identify which protein fraction is altered.
special: Albumin/globulin values or electrophoresis may be requested when indicated.
related: Hydration can influence concentration measurements.

name: Ionised Calcium
measure: Measures physiologically active unbound calcium in blood.
why: Assessment of calcium imbalance in relevant settings.
fasting: Fasting is usually not required; follow specimen-handling instructions.
limitation: Ionised calcium is sensitive to specimen pH and collection/handling delays.
special: Ionised calcium differs from total calcium, especially with abnormal albumin or acid-base status.
related: Prompt specimen transport is important for reliable measurement.
